title: Licences in practice: AGPL, GPL, MIT, OpenRAIL

questions.q: You change a GPL-3.0 pack and use it only on your own machine. Does the source duty apply?
options: Only if it is a node pack
questions.why: The duties attach to conveying a copy.

questions.q: What does AGPL-3.0 add to GPL-3.0?
options: An offer of source to remote users of a modified version
A requirement to publish your pictures
questions.answer: An offer of source to remote users of a modified version

questions.q: You run an unmodified AGPL-3.0 pack on a website. Does section 13 ask anything of you?
options: Not by its words, since it says if you modify
questions.answer: Not by its words, since it says if you modify
questions.why: Section 13 begins with modifying the program. This is a reading, not legal advice.

questions.q: Which of these applies at home, with nothing shared?
questions.why: Its use restrictions apply to use itself.

questions.q: You find a useful pack with no licence. What does that generally mean?
options: You have no permission to use, modify or share it
You can use it if you credit the author
questions.answer: You have no permission to use, modify or share it
questions.why: As choosealicense.com puts it. Ask the author, or write your own.

questions.q: What is the one condition of the MIT licence?
options: Keep the copyright and permission notice
questions.answer: Keep the copyright and permission notice
questions.why: In all copies or substantial portions.
